newsitem.title: USA: U.S. exporters cannot confirm China soymeal talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. exporters cannot confirm China soymeal talk.

text.p: Several U.S. exporters on Tuesday could not confirm market talk that China bought several soymeal cargoes of South American origin.
"I would be very surprised to see it, unless it was for a much, much deferred position," one U.S. exporter said.

Chicago Board of Trade soymeal futures ended lower on Tuesday amid talk China had purchased South American supplies. Floor sources cited talk China bought two to three cargoes of South American soymeal.

"My latest information from China is that the ports are all congested with an estimated one million tonnes of soybean meal that needs to be unloaded and there does not seem to be a great deal of market for this meal," he said.
Another exporter said there was some evidence of Chinese buying interest on Tuesday.

"But nobody is going to know. The important thing is with the board dropping, it is likely to uncover some buying interest. There has been some cash buying of meal in South America and that would support the possibility that some meal had been traded," he said.
Some exporters said they do not see China aggressively importing meal at least for the short term because it seems to have ample supply.
"They have good supplies," a third U.S. exporter said. "South American meal is coming on stream and is much cheaper than U.S. soymeal," he said.

Also, the United States has a very tight carryout. The U.S. Agriculture Department forecast in its April report that only 125 million bushels of soybeans would be on hand at the end of August -- the smallest stocks figure since 1976/77.
"It is hard to figure out from Chicago," the exporter said, referring to the reported Chinese purchase.
Exporters said they expect the Chinese to be buying summer positions out of South America at some point. "So it is entirely feasible. I really do not know," one said.
